meta.description: Table health expectations to validate that optimization has been applied. Run after OPTIMIZE / Liquid Clustering / bloom filter creation to verify the table is in a healthy state for query performance.
meta.when_to_run: After OPTIMIZE completes. Alert if avg_file_size_mb < 64 (small file problem persists) or num_files has grown beyond threshold.

meta.notes: OPTIMIZE must not produce an empty table. Failure here indicates a corrupt or empty source.
Replace 'partition_col' with your actual partition column. NULL partition values cause data to land in the __HIVE_DEFAULT_PARTITION__ partition — a common source of small files and query plan issues.
Run DESCRIBE DETAIL and compute avg_file_size_mb = sizeInBytes / 1024 / 1024 / numFiles. Values < 64 MB indicate small file problem; > 1024 MB may cause task OOM. Adjust bounds for your workload.
Tables with > 50K files suffer from slow file listing. If breached, switch to Liquid Clustering or increase OPTIMIZE frequency.
Replace 'bloom_filter_col' with the column you created a bloom filter on (e.g., user_id). Bloom filters do not help NULL values — if NULLs are frequent, fix upstream data quality.
Replace 'clustering_col' with your CLUSTER BY or ZORDER BY column. NULL clustering keys are stored in separate files and cannot be skipped by data-skipping stats.
